# Guardian crypto fixtures

- `dkg-three-of-four.txt` is generated by the independent affine integer arithmetic in `generate_dkg.py`. It uses only the numbered curve/generator definitions in `spec/02-cryptography.md`; it neither reads nor imports implementation source or the spec verification scripts. Its five keys cover aggregate secret 5 and all four shares of the public test polynomial `5+7*x+11*x²`, with `x=id+1`. The generator also checks the negative G2 point used by the Rust tests is on-curve and outside the order-r subgroup.
- Mint G1 mappings and the two-share interpolation/pairing fixtures in `tests/crypto.rs` are literal public vectors from `spec/verification/core/implementation-vectors.json` (baseline `0c316439d60b5a08eea26fab216780eb893c45bf`). No baseline implementation was consulted.
- BIP340 vector zero is from the [Bitcoin BIP340 vector CSV](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0340/test-vectors.csv). SHA256 `abc` and HMAC-SHA512 `Hi There` are standard SHA/RFC4231 known answers.
- The zero-seeded scalar uses the published original ChaCha20 zero-key/IV first block `76b8e0ad…b2ee6586`, interpreted little-endian and reduced modulo r using Python integers. Message-mapping vectors additionally exercise stream continuation, sign consumption, field-half significance and cofactor clearing.

The polynomial coefficients and secret key values are deliberately public test inputs. These checks establish primitive conformance, not a complete distributed DKG transcript or process interoperability.

Regenerate/check public DKG keys:

```sh
nix-shell --run 'python3 tests/fixtures/crypto/generate_dkg.py > /tmp/minimint-dkg-generated.txt && cmp /tmp/minimint-dkg-generated.txt tests/fixtures/crypto/dkg-three-of-four.txt'
```

Native public APIs were validated against blst 0.3.17 generated bindings, k256 0.14.0 documentation, and OpenSSL 0.10.81 documentation. OpenSSL's [EVP_chacha20 documentation](https://docs.openssl.org/3.0/man3/EVP_chacha20/) explicitly specifies a little-endian 64-bit counter followed by a 64-bit nonce. Secret arithmetic uses blst/k256; OpenSSL BigNums in the custom mapping operate only on public message-derived field values.
